AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Dr. Mara Vey
The news networks are calling it the Grey Bloom now. I suppose it needed a name people could understand. I walked through South Industrial today.
I recognized the growth pattern immediately, not because it looks like our cultivation chambers—it doesn't anymore—but the recovery behavior is still there.

Cut it. It regrows. Dry it. Dormant material survives. Remove one colony and another appears where infrastructure is already compromised. This is Evercrop. Changed by scale. Changed by environment. But ours.
The crop that refuses to fail. I wish I had never said those words.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Municipal Emergency Worker
People outside think the city is dead. It isn't. That's what makes this hard. Trains still run sometimes. Restaurants are open north of the river. Two schools reopened last week.

The hospital is still taking patients. Crews still patch water mains. People still argue about rent. Then you turn a corner and an entire warehouse block is white-grey growth and military engineers are preparing to burn it.
It isn't apocalypse. Not yet. It's Tuesday, except part of Tuesday is trying to eat the electrical grid.
If everything ended at once we'd know it was over. Instead we keep waking up and trying again.
